title: replace a historical manufacturing visual-inspection model
input: The quality team retains labeled normal and defective images and its capture conditions.
action: Lookout for Vision historically trained and invoked image anomaly models for visual inspection. Revalidate any replacement against the same defect classes, lighting and camera geometry before it controls inspection decisions.
output: The inspection application routes uncertain or defective items to the approved human review path.
check: Measure known-defect recall, false rejects and capture-condition changes using the retained acceptance dataset.

title: submit a permitted blockchain operation through a managed access path
input: The application prepares a signed transaction or authorized query for its selected blockchain network.
action: Managed Blockchain's selected network or access feature supplies supported blockchain infrastructure access. Network-specific validation and consensus determine accepted ledger state; the application protects signing keys and interprets confirmation status.
output: The application reconciles the submitted transaction with the network's resulting ledger state.
check: Check network support, signing-key custody and confirmation handling; submission success is not final settlement.

title: visualize application metrics from authorized data sources
input: The operations owner selects data-source endpoints, dashboard queries and viewer roles.
action: Managed Grafana runs the Grafana workspace and queries configured data sources under their authorized credentials. Panels visualize returned metrics or logs; the workspace is not the primary telemetry collector or application processor.
output: The on-call engineer inspects latency and error panels to narrow the incident and consults source evidence.
check: Check query scope, data freshness, viewer permissions and dashboard behavior when a data source is unavailable.

service: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
title: calculate event-time sales aggregates from a stream
input: The producer emits sale events with timestamps and stable event identifiers to the approved stream.
action: Managed Service for Apache Flink runs the configured Flink application, which parses events, applies event-time windows and maintains operator state. Checkpoint and sink semantics determine restart and duplicate handling.
output: The sink stores the computed sales aggregates for the dashboard query path.
check: Test late events, duplicate inputs, checkpoint recovery and sink consistency before trusting the displayed totals.

title: query scraped Kubernetes workload metrics
input: The platform owner configures approved Prometheus-compatible collectors and remote-write credentials.
action: Managed Service for Prometheus ingests permitted remote-write samples into a workspace and supports PromQL queries and configured rules. Collectors scrape the workloads; the service stores and evaluates their metric samples.
output: The Grafana workspace or alert receiver uses query and rule results to detect an operational issue.
check: Check label cardinality, scrape coverage, query permissions and missing-sample behavior before relying on alerts.

service: Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow
title: orchestrate a nightly data pipeline with retryable tasks
input: The data engineer publishes DAG code and dependencies for the scheduled warehouse update.
action: MWAA supplies the managed Airflow environment that schedules DAG tasks and runs their configured operators. Operators invoke extraction or transformation jobs; Airflow tracks task dependencies and state rather than storing the warehouse dataset.
output: The pipeline's final task publishes the accepted warehouse partition after upstream jobs and quality gates succeed.
check: Test task retries, backfill idempotency, secret access and a failed upstream dependency before enabling the schedule.

title: collect reviewed human labels for a training dataset
input: The dataset owner prepares approved labeling tasks, worker requirements and evaluation examples.
action: Mechanical Turk distributes human intelligence tasks to eligible workers and collects submitted assignments. Workers provide labels; qualification and acceptance policies control which assignments become training evidence.
output: The dataset curator checks agreement and accepts only suitable labels into the versioned training dataset.
check: Use known-answer items, worker-quality checks and privacy review before paying for and importing labels.

title: store application session state in a durable in-memory database
input: The application submits authorized session updates and stable keys with explicit expiry policy.
action: MemoryDB serves supported Redis-compatible data operations using its configured cluster and durability architecture. Clients handle endpoint discovery and retry ambiguity; application key design determines session ownership and expiration.
output: The session backend reads the current permitted session state and returns the authorized application context.
check: Test failover, expiry, concurrent writes and replay behavior without allowing cross-user key access.

title: investigate graph relationships in a fraud dataset
input: The analyst imports an approved graph of accounts, devices and transactions.
action: Neptune Analytics executes supported graph queries and algorithms against the loaded analytical graph. Traversals or similarity analysis identify relationships; analysts validate whether a relationship indicates suspicious behavior.
output: The investigation application presents relevant paths and algorithm results as evidence for a reviewer.
check: Check graph version, edge meaning, query access and known reference paths before escalating a case.

title: classify a customer document with a selected foundation model
input: The application submits the permitted document input to a supported Nova model through Bedrock.
action: The selected Nova model generates the requested classification or extraction response from the supplied input. Supported modalities and model settings bound the invocation; application code validates the response schema and business meaning.
output: The document handler accepts validated fields and routes uncertain or unsupported output for review.
check: Evaluate representative documents, prompt injection, schema errors and sensitive-input policy before release.
